note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank or banking association ranking was read): Ziraat Bankası, Türkiye İş Bankası and Garanti BBVA. İş Bankası's and Garanti BBVA's fee pages answered not found at the addresses tried, Yapı Kredi's didn't answer and its Worldcard rates page answered not found behind a captcha; a search found Garanti's fees only on comparison sites and in complaints, which aren't sources. Ziraat Bankası's Bankkart rates and fees page, read in full on 2026-10-30 (its rows updated between 15 December 2022 and 9 March 2026): every personal Ziraat credit card is written: the Prestij and Prestij Plus at 1,880 lira a year, the Gold 384, the Classic 222, the Platinum 462 and the Ücretsiz (free) card nothing, each fee including the banking tax (BSMV) where the row says so. Each bears contractual interest of 3.25% a month on a period's debt under 30,000 lira, 3.75% to 180,000 and 4.25% above, the central bank's ceilings (in force from 1 November 2026 at the same figures, read on 2026-10-29); the rate steps with the balance, which the game's card holds as one rate, so the first step is written. Cash advances bear 4.25% a month, and a domestic cash advance costs 1% where the card's rows give it (other banks' ATMs add 2.87% plus 0.57 lira, not written); the default interest (gecikme faizi) of 3.55% a month on a period's debt under 30,000 lira is written as the penalty rate. The page gives no minimum payment, grace period or foreign transaction fee. The youth card (Genç), the Başak producer cards and the business cards aren't written: the youth card's fee is printed as a dash, and the others aren't personal cards.
